answer: Threshold-signature vouching requires each new identity to obtain t-of-n member signatures bound to its pubkey and epoch seed. Joint liability is key: if a vouched identity is a clone, every sponsor forfeits stake. A farmer with many keys hits a recursive wall: each clone needs t fresh sponsors who refuse to back unverifiable clusters. A terrace of stacked endorsements cannot be faked since the threshold demands distinct staked keys. A beacon each epoch lists sponsors and their load. As the network pulse advances, sponsors with poor records lose weight, making cloning costly at entry.
